stories.headline: Government approves €10bn Piano Casa housing plan; cabinet erupts in Salvini-Giuli clash; accise extension tacked on
stories.summary: The Council of Ministers on 30 April approved a housing decree allocating up to €10 billion over ten years to create 100,000 dwellings, including fast-tracked eviction procedures and notary fee reductions. The session was overshadowed by a shouting match between Deputy PM Salvini, who demanded the heritage superintendencies be bypassed for fast construction in historic centres, and Culture Minister Giuli, who threatened to vote against the plan; Meloni intervened with 'basta spocchia.' The same press conference also announced a three-week extension of the fuel excise-duty cut.

stories.headline: Trump threatens to withdraw US troops from Italy and Spain; Crosetto expresses bewilderment
stories.summary: US President Trump, citing Italy's failure to support US operations against Iran, said a troop withdrawal from Italy was 'probable,' targeting the roughly 13,000 US personnel at bases including Aviano, Sigonella, and Naples. Defence Minister Crosetto publicly stated he would not understand the rationale, noting Italy had offered naval protection for Hormuz shipping; Meloni and the government were otherwise cautious. Opposition parties demanded a firmer response. The story ran parallel to broader reporting on US troop drawdowns in Germany and Europe-wide NATO tensions.

stories.headline: US Secretary of State Rubio to visit Rome next week for Italy-US and Vatican diplomatic reset
stories.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio is scheduled to visit Rome on 7–8 May, with confirmed appointments at the Vatican (Pope Leone XIV and Cardinal Parolin) and meetings with Foreign Minister Tajani and Defence Minister Crosetto; an encounter with PM Meloni is described as possible but not confirmed. Coverage frames the visit as a bid to repair tensions that have built since Trump criticised Meloni and the Vatican. The trip coincides with Trump's reposting of a Salvini interview praising him — widely read as signalling a US preference for Salvini over Meloni.

stories.headline: Trump reposts Salvini's Breitbart interview praising him, signalling preference over Meloni
stories.summary: Trump shared on Truth Social a February Breitbart interview in which Salvini praised Trump's 'courage and cultural foundations,' with the repost occurring on the day Rubio's Rome visit was announced. Italian media read it as a deliberate diplomatic snub to Meloni, who has faced cooling relations with Washington since criticising Israeli actions. Salvini separately praised the repost; the episode is widely framed as underlining a rift within Italy's governing coalition over the US relationship.

stories.headline: Tajani holds multiple calls with Iranian FM Araghchi on Hormuz, nuclear red lines, and ceasefire
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Tajani spoke by phone with his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi at least twice in the space of days, conveying Italy's strong concern over rising Middle East tensions, stating that Iranian military nuclear development is an Italian 'red line,' and calling for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Italy also raised readiness to assist Gulf states and offered to participate in post-conflict demining of Hormuz. Araghchi reportedly replied that some European countries were not being constructive on the nuclear file.

stories.headline: Israel seizes Gaza Flotilla vessels; Italian activists detained and reportedly mistreated; government calls for immediate release
stories.summary: Israeli forces boarded ships of the Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters near Crete; 24 Italian nationals were among those detained. The Italian government held an emergency meeting chaired by Meloni, who called on Israel to respect international law and release the Italians. Two activists, Thiago Avila and Saif Abukeshek, had their detention extended by two days and appeared in court in chains. Opposition parties accused the government of inaction and demanded it break with Netanyahu. Tajani activated the Crisis Unit and Italian embassies in Tel Aviv and Athens.

stories.headline: Meloni government marks second-longest tenure in Republic's history as polls show governing coalition slipping behind
stories.summary: On 2 May PM Meloni announced her government had surpassed 1,288 days in office, becoming the second-longest-serving executive in the Italian Republic's history. She framed it as a 'responsibility, not a milestone.' Simultaneously, multiple polls showed FdI declining (to around 28–29%), Lega at or near 7%, and the broad centre-left 'campo largo' drawing level with or overtaking the governing coalition in hypothetical elections, prompting sharp commentary from opposition leader Schlein and commentary from analysts that the government's political energy is exhausted.

stories.headline: Minetti presidential pardon scandal engulfs Justice Minister Nordio and touches Mattarella
stories.summary: A presidential pardon granted in February to Nicole Minetti — convicted for facilitating prostitution in the 'Bunga Bunga' era — blew into a major political controversy after Il Fatto Quotidiano reported that key facts in the pardon application (notably an alleged adoption) were false. President Mattarella wrote urgently to Justice Minister Nordio demanding verification; the Milan Court of Appeal's general prosecutor launched inquiries. The PD demanded Nordio's resignation, FdI blamed a former Nordio chief of staff, and Meloni expressed trust in Nordio while distancing herself from the file. The case ran for over a week with multiple constitutional analyses of whether a pardon can be revoked.
